## What I built

A real CSV state-machine parser and serializer in MoonBit, following RFC 4180 as adapted by `specs/csv.md`. The `declare`d API in `csv_spec.mbt` is implemented in `csv.mbt`, delegating to focused modules:

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `parser.mbt` | `Parser` cursor + field/record/consistency state machines |
| `scanner.mbt` | UTF‑16 code-unit predicates (`is_record_terminator`) |

| `error.mbt` | `ParseError` suberror + `message` |
| `csv.mbt` | public `parse` / `print` entry points |

## Key correctness points

- **32-bit `Int` trap found and fixed**: MoonBit `Int` is 32-bit, so the Huffman bit accumulator and the integer decoder use `Int64` — otherwise concatenated 30-bit codes and continuation octets silently overflowed.

- Huffman: EOS, >7-bit padding, and non-ones padding all raise `InvalidHuffman`.
- Size updates are legal only before the first field, capped by the decoder limit, and signalled by the encoder as smallest-then-final.

## INI parser — complete

Implemented a genuine, line-based INI parser for the `tonyfettes/ini` package. `@ini.parse` / `@ini.print` are provided in the root package, satisfying the declarations in `ini_spec.mbt`.

### Structure
- `ini.mbt` — public entry point `parse` + a `ParseError` sub-error; the single-pass line walk that fills `global`/`sections`.
- `scanner.mbt` — line splitting, CRLF handling, trailing-backslash counting, inline-comment detection, separator lookup, and per-carrier escape decoding.
- `parser.mbt` — section-header parsing, key validation, continuation assembly, quoted/unquoted value parsing.
- `printer.mbt` — `print` and value/section encoding.
- `ini_edge_test.mbt` — 71 additional black-box tests derived from `specs/ini.md`.
- `README.md` — architecture, algorithms, usage, testing, design decisions.

### Behavior implemented (per `specs/ini.md`)
First `=`/`:` separator (so URLs/colons in values survive); trimmed keys/unquoted values; control-char keys rejected; duplicate keys last-wins and section re-open; full-line and whitespace-guarded inline `;`/`#` comments; `"…"`/`'…'` quoted values closing on the same line with inner whitespace/comment markers preserved; the per-carrier escape table (`\\ \n \r \t`, double adds `\"`, single only `\\`/`\'`, everything else verbatim so `C:\Program` works); continuations decided on raw text by odd/even trailing-backslash run; LF and CRLF; and rejection of malformed headers, missing separators, empty/whitespace keys, unterminated/mismatched quotes, text after a closing quote, and dangling continuations.

`print` writes every value in double quotes (the one carrier that preserves any value), so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds; a quickcheck property test plus a 1500-case "parse never panics" fuzz confirm it.

### Independent audit and fix
An independent audit flagged one real defect: a dangling continuation marker at end of input (`key=value\` followed by a line break) was silently accepted because a trailing LF left an artifact empty split element that got joined. Fixed in `split_lines` (drop the trailing empty element when input ends in LF), so a marker with no real following line now raises — matching the spec's "A marker with no line after it is invalid" for `key=value\`, `key=value\\n`, the CRLF form, and after earlier entries, while markers followed by real lines still join. Added regression tests for all those shapes.

- `moon check` → 0 errors; the only warnings are pre-existing ones from the given files I must not modify (`ini_spec.mbt`, `ini_qc.mbt`, `ini_pub_test.mbt`); no warnings originate from my implementation or tests. `moon.pkg` was tidied so `core/test` is a proper `for "test"` import.

## What was built

## Key design points

- **Line scanner** → blank lines, `;`/`#` full-line comments, `[section]` headers, and key/value entries, all line-based.
- **Sections** — strict `[name]` with only trailing whitespace, rejection of `[`/`]` nesting, empty/whitespace-only names, and stripping of one wrapping quote pair (`["quoted name"]` → `quoted name`, while `[remote "origin"]` keeps its quotes).

- **Continuations** — decided on the raw trailing-backslash run *before* escaping, so an odd run marks a join and an even run is escaped literals (the documented N=1..4 table), with a dangling marker rejected.
- **Printer** — always double-quotes, escaping exactly `\ " \n \r \t`; `parse(print(doc)) == doc` is verified by the 300-case property test plus my extra round-trips.

## Key correctness points

- **Streaming:** every value is gathered through `read_exactly`, so all readers work over a one-byte-per-call `Reader`; end of stream inside a value raises.
- **Varints:** non-minimal encodings accepted, `80×9 7F` = 2^63, eleventh byte raises; 32-bit readers keep the low 32 bits.
- **Lengths:** the full varint is bounded to `0 ..= 2^31-1`, so `2^32` (low 32 bits zero) is rejected.
- **Floats/doubles:** raw bit reinterpretation, so NaN payloads, infinities and `-0.0` round-trip bit-exactly (verified).
- **Packed fields:** decoded through a `LimitedReader` window; a payload ending mid-element raises.
- **Unknown fields/groups:** all wire types skipped; nested groups handled with an explicit stack, raising on mismatched end tags and on wire type 4/6/7.

Design highlights: a **single-pass recursive-descent parser**; input normalized once (CRLF→LF) so a surviving CR is simply an illegal control character; ordinary text **copied by slice** so non-BMP characters survive in parser *and* printer; structural rules expressed as two per-path facts (**frozen** and **explicit nest**) stored in a tree that mirrors the document paths, with **deferred commits** for dotted keys so `a.b = 1` / `a.c = 2` stays valid while a later `[a]` is rejected.

## Key approach

- **Splitting** runs outside-in (fragment → query → scheme → authority/path) mirroring the grammar, with first-match-wins scheme detection and the Section 4.2 no-colon-in-first-segment rule for relative references.
- **Validation** is a direct transcription of the ABNF, so forbidden characters, malformed `pct-encoded` triplets, non-numeric ports, mismatched brackets/IP-literals, ambiguous authorities (second `@`, stray text after `]`), and invalid schemes all fall out naturally.
- **IPv6** is validated by counting 16-bit groups around a single `::` (exactly 8 without it, ≤7 across it), with dotted IPv4 only allowed as the final group — provably equivalent to the nine ABNF alternatives.
- **Resolution** is strict Section 5.2 with the RFC's literal two-buffer dot-segment algorithm, so all Section 5.4 normal and abnormal examples come out right (verified in tests).
